channel.title: Arya Somu · Writing
channel.description: Notes and essays by Arya Somu, published on aryasomu.com.

item.title: Introducing TrainKernel
item.description: An experimental compiler turns a supported PyTorch training step into one cooperative CUDA megakernel. A detailed look at its design, A100 and H100 benchmarks, use cases, and limits.

item.title: The price of compute, the price of power
item.description: A ten-year model of useful compute and delivered power, with Texas, Alberta, Québec, and PJM as case studies in location, flexibility, and the emerging market for compute.

item.title: The promise of a green light
item.description: Four traffic-light controllers reveal the difference between avoiding a conflict, guaranteeing progress, and deciding who waits. Includes an interactive model and recorded walkthrough.

item.title: Molecular origami
item.description: A small-budget Qwen3-8B RNA inverse-folding experiment with reinforcement learning, classical controls, and a numerical audit.

item.title: How many independent forecasts are in a crowd?
item.description: A frozen synthetic study of shared evidence, scalar pooling failure, and learning source groups from resolved forecasts.

item.title: I taught Nemotron to flip graph edges. A small search still wins.
item.description: A Nemotron 4B adapter learned useful local moves on two small book-graph repair tasks. Exact CPU search remained stronger, and no new Ramsey bound was found.

item.title: I post-trained Nemotron 4B into an Average Banker
item.description: A one-epoch adapter doubled Nemotron's accuracy on a narrow banking-support intent test, with a synthetic false start and limits on what that score means.

item.title: What should an AI ask when every explanation fits?
item.description: A conversational account of exact causal experiment choice, locked model tests, and what changed when an agent received an exact-risk calculator.

item.title: The Typical Path of a Favorable Bet
item.description: A fixed-seed experiment shows how a favorable repeated bet can raise expected wealth while leaving the median bankroll poorer. Filed under September 18, 2026; first published October 11, 2026.

item.title: The Epistemic Century
item.description: How AI could change the institutions that generate, test, fund, and act on claims. Originally published on Substack July 9, 2026; added to this site October 11, 2026.

item.title: When 95% credible intervals cover 81%
item.description: A derivation and reproducible simulation of posterior coverage under model misspecification.
